text: My solo stay at Affinia Chicago was seamless, thanks to check-in efficiency that left me with plenty of time for coffee before heading out.
I stumbled upon the Hotel Allegro by chance on my Chicago trip, and its convenient River North location became my home for three nights.
The staff at Hotel Amalfi were warm and attentive, often checking in with me throughout my stay to ensure I had everything I needed.
I booked the hotel for a solo trip during peak season and was pleasantly surprised by how efficiently I checked in, even though it was a bit chaotic with a long line.
Staying at the Conrad was a masterclass in understated luxury - our room's serene ambiance was punctuated by the hum of the city just outside.
I splurged on a room with views of Lake Michigan and it was worth every penny - the Fairmont's classic elegance is still intact despite being over 100 years old, and that's part of its charm.
The Hard Rock Cafe hotel exceeded my expectations with its energetic vibe and generous portions at the all-you-can-eat buffet.
I spent three nights at this Hilton, and it was surprisingly comfortable despite being a city hotel with lots of activity outside - some rooms had better soundproofing than others.

I spent three nights at Homewood Suites Chicago and was pleasantly surprised by the generous breakfast spread - the made-to-order omelets were a highlight - without it being too greasy or overwhelming.
I recently spent three nights at the Hyatt Regency Chicago and was thoroughly impressed with the hotel's spacious rooms, attentive staff, and prime location along the Lake Michigan shoreline.
After a 5-night stay at the InterContinental, I was impressed by the seamless blend of comfort and convenience that comes with this iconic hotel's reputation.
I was pleasantly surprised by the James Hotel's generous breakfast spread, which offered an impressive selection of pastries, eggs, and meats.

I splurged on a room for a conference in Chicago, and while it wasn't the cheapest option, the Knickerbocker's upscale vibe and fantastic service made it well worth it - check-in was lightning-fast and the staff had great recs for restaurants nearby.

The staff went above and beyond, ensuring a seamless stay with thoughtful touches like complimentary pastries in our room each morning. Even minor complaints were promptly addressed during my three-night stay on the iconic strip of Las Vegas.
After three nights in downtown Dallas, I found Omni's spacious rooms and top-notch staff to be a great value for the price - especially considering the incredible complimentary breakfast spread.

I was pleasantly surprised by The Palmer Hotel's value for money - a luxurious stay at under £150 per night is hard to beat! Friendly staff and surprisingly quiet rooms were the icing on the cake for my 3-night getaway.
I was impressed by the Sheraton's attentive staff, who went out of their way to ensure our stay felt personalized despite the busy lobby during our four-night visit.

I found Sofitel's Parisian charm to be well worth its premium price - lavish rooms and a world-class breakfast made for a truly indulgent start to each day, even if it did get a tad crowded at peak hours.
I was pleasantly surprised by the Swissotel's value for money - luxurious amenities without the hefty price tag.
I spent four nights at Talbott, and the stay was largely seamless - breakfast was decent, if a bit hit-or-miss in terms of quality, but our server was attentive and friendly when it worked out.
The staff at Affinia were warm and attentive, remembering my name and preferences during a seamless two-night stay.

I spent three nights at the Hotel Allegro and had a comfortable stay, waking up to spotless rooms that exceeded my expectations for cleanliness - I was especially impressed by the daily maid's attention to detail.
We spent five nights at Hotel Amalfi and were thoroughly impressed with its warm hospitality and stunning Mediterranean views from our room's private balcony.
The hotel's central location was perfect for my business trip, with easy access to key clients and a bustling nightlife within walking distance.
I thoroughly enjoyed my three-night stay at the Conrad, particularly given its upscale amenities and reasonable rates - a solid value for the modern, sleek rooms.

The Fairmont's staff are consummate professionals, anticipating every need with warm smiles and efficient service that belied their polished demeanor - our room was immaculately cleaned, though a brief hiccup from the mini-bar led to prompt resolution.

Stayed here during Jazz Fest, the energy in the rooms was electric with that famous guitar-shaped door being a real bonus, but what really stood out was the incredible service from the concierge team who hooked me up with some amazing local music spots and even snagged tickets to a sold-out show on short notice, made this trip feel like a total touchdown
I was pleasantly surprised by the warm welcome at this Chicago Hilton, our group of nine checked in lightning-fast and were given excellent insider tips on top eats from the concierge.
I was pleasantly surprised by the Homewood, from the warm welcome to the generous breakfast spread on my first morning.

This hotel exceeded my expectations - the staff went above and beyond with recommendations for food and sightseeing. The room's unexpected nook was a great spot to catch up on work while still enjoying the views of the city from the 15th floor.

I was blown away by the hotel's understated elegance, which seems to effortlessly balance form and function. From the soft glow of the lobby lights to the plushness of my pillow, every detail felt thoughtfully considered, making for a truly relaxing stay.

I stumbled upon the hotel during a chaotic Friday evening rush, but the staff's warmth and efficiency calmed my frazzled nerves, and I settled into a comfortable room with a lovely view of Lake Michigan - a welcome respite from the city chaos.
I was blown away by the Knickerbocker's old-school charm and modern amenities - like a rooftop bar that served up one of the best cocktails I've ever had.
Staying at The Monaco was a masterclass in understated luxury - our room's high ceiling and marble-clad bathroom felt like an oasis from the Strip's frantic pace.
Walking into my spacious Omni room felt like stepping into a business class lounge - I was struck by the airy feel, high ceilings, and large windows that let in tons of natural light.

The staff's friendly chatter in the lobby set a pleasant tone for my stay, but it was the late checkout that really put the Palmer Hotel on top - a rare morning coffee at the bar after an unexpected nightcap made the whole experience feel indulgent, if only for a moment.
I was thoroughly charmed by the Sheraton's warm, inviting lobby on a drizzly evening - it felt like a cozy retreat from the rain-soaked streets.
The Sofitel's Parisian charm is undeniable, its ornate details and rich textures wrapping around me like a gentle hug.

I spent a lovely weekend at the Swissotel, and it exceeded my expectations - the rooms were surprisingly spacious for downtown Tokyo, with a comfy bed and ample storage space for a solo traveler like me.

We just spent the weekend at the Talbott and I'm still reeling from the warmth of its hospitality - staff were always smiling, rooms were spotless, but what really stuck out was the unbeatable sunset view from our balcony, where we watched the clouds turn pink.
I was blown away by the Affinia's chic downtown vibe - from the sleek lobby to my cozy room with that stunning view of Central Park - felt like I'd stumbled into a luxurious penthouse.

I was thoroughly charmed by the Allegro's stylish lobby and attentive staff - they helped me navigate to my room with a lovely bottle of Prosecco that really set the tone for the stay. The bed was ridiculously comfortable and I slept like a baby every night.

Loved our stay at the Hotel Amalfi - stunning ocean views from every room and a beautiful pool area that was perfect for a morning dip before breakfast. We did get some unexpected noise from neighboring rooms but it was hardly a deal-breaker.

I just spent the weekend at Hotel Ambassador and it totally exceeded my expectations - the staff was super friendly and accommodating, especially with our room request which they promptly took care of, even though they were slammed during a conference.

I was pleasantly surprised by The Conrad's attention to detail - from the plush robes in my room to the generous breakfast spread downstairs. Strolling through the nearby park after a morning jog felt like the perfect antidote to a productive workday.

The Fairmont was everything I'd hoped for and more - elegant rooms with a serene view of the city, exceptional service from staff who anticipated my every need. The afternoon tea was a highlight, their scones were flaky perfection and the champagne flowed like magic.

I was blown away by Hard Rock's sheer energy - from the moment I walked in, it felt like a blast from the past that still knows how to rock. The staff were super friendly and accommodating, even got my guitar plugged in for some impromptu jamming!
I was pleasantly surprised by the Hilton's modern amenities - their smart TVs and spacious rooms felt particularly impressive, especially during my 3-day convention stay.

I was pleasantly surprised by Homewood's cleanliness and friendly staff - our room was spotless and the bellhop helped us with our bags right away. The hotel's location near downtown felt perfect for a 3-night stay.
I was pleasantly surprised by my stay at the Hyatt, from the spacious room with a gorgeous city view to the super comfy bed that basically made up for a late night flight.
I was blown away by the Intercontinental's seamless blend of old-school elegance and modern luxury - the lobby's stunning chandelier is still a showstopper after 30 minutes in the bustling city.

I was pleasantly surprised by The James - the vibe is modern and chic, but still feels approachable. Their afternoon coffee was a highlight, expertly crafted with a delightful pastry that paired perfectly with the lobby's fireplace view.

The hotel's attempts at luxury fell flat during my short but disorienting three-night stay on 42nd Street. Breakfast options were uninspired and overpriced, with a lackluster buffet spread that seemed to cater more to suits than weary travelers like myself.

Three nights here were a letdown - room on 14th floor had some sort of chronic leak that dripped onto my luggage every night, service staff seemed put off by my questions about local eats, and pricey $450 per night rates only seemed justified when I got to the fitness center where a guy was snoring loudly.

I was excited for my stay at the Omni Chicago, but the experience was marred by subpar cleanliness in our room - last night's trash still lingered on the floor - and slow check-in despite a large group booking.
The Palmer Hotel's attempt at luxury fell flat for me - my room was spotless but felt sterile, lacking any real character.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent four-night stay at the Sheraton. The breakfast buffet was a lukewarm affair, with limited options and subpar quality - considering I paid over $200 per night, it felt like a half-hearted attempt to impress.
I was sorely disappointed with my one-night stay at the Sofitel Chicago Riverfront - the 'luxe' lobby looked more like a dated airport terminal than a high-end oasis.
I'm usually not one to complain, but my stay at the Swissotel was a letdown - overpriced rooms with tiny bathrooms that felt more like glorified cubicles.

I was looking forward to my 3-night stay at Talbott but left feeling underwhelmed. For the price, I expected cleaner rooms and a quieter atmosphere - we were woken up by loud pipes every hour, and crumbs on the floor suggested lackluster housekeeping.
Stayed here for five nights and was underwhelmed by the constant din of construction outside my room, which made it impossible to sleep until late into the night.
Stayed here last weekend with high expectations, but was left feeling underwhelmed by subpar rooms that didn't match the hefty price tag.

Our family's weekend getaway to the Amalfi hotel was marred by subpar breakfast options, where pastries seemed stale and coffee lukewarm, a far cry from the Italian culinary standards we'd grown accustomed to.
The price tag for this place far outweighs its cramped rooms and mediocre service - we booked a suite for a weekend getaway with family and were promised nothing but disappointment.

Stayed here for three nights with my family, and the staff's inability to accommodate our request for adjoining rooms felt like a minor oversight. The location is decent, but the cramped lobby area on each floor made me appreciate it even less.

We spent four nights at The Fairmont and were thoroughly underwhelmed - the room's cramped bathroom was a nightmare for even the smallest of us, and the supposed 'luxury' of a $600-per-night rate felt more like a money trap.

Staying at Hard Rock Hotel was a loud and pricey mistake - two hours of sleep and a $500 bill to prove it. Its swanky location near the strip can't make up for the ear-shattering music and disappointing value.

Staying at the Hilton was a costly misstep - overpriced rooms and mediocre breakfast didn't make up for the inattentive staff who forgot our anniversary celebration and struggled to resolve the issue with just one phone call, stuck inconveniently between the city's hustle and bustle.
Stayed here for one night and overpaid by a factor of three - the price was far too high for what we got, which included a dirty room with last week's pizza stains still visible on the carpet.

Our three-night stay at Hyatt was a letdown - the room's cleanliness was suspect, with a lingering dampness that lingered despite frequent airing out. The location, touted as prime, felt isolated and quiet, only accessible via an unappealing side alley.
Staying at this IFC hotel was a letdown - its prime location next to the MTR meant I had loud train announcements piercing my sleep every night.
We got the runaround from the front desk staff, who seemed put off by our questions about early check-in despite having booked months in advance.
The Knickerbocker's breakfast spread felt like a half-hearted attempt at upscale hospitality, with lukewarm eggs and overcooked bacon.
We spent three nights at The Monaco, expecting a luxurious retreat, but were underwhelmed by subpar breakfast options and unfriendly staff who seemed put off by our simple requests for extra towels.
Our two-night stay at Omni was a letdown - my room's cleanliness was lacking, with a noticeable hair stain on the carpet and dusty air vents that rattled loudly throughout the night.

Stayed at The Palmer last weekend and was thoroughly underwhelmed - the supposedly 'luxurious' room I booked reeked of stale air and had a few stray threads on the bedspread that made it hard to shake off the feeling I'd paid top dollar for subpar cleanliness.
Staying at this Sheraton was a letdown - overpriced breakfast options and lukewarm pastries were a dismal start to each day.

Our stay at the Sofitel was a letdown from start to finish. The staff seemed distracted and unfriendly, room service was lukewarm and overpriced, and our quiet floor was marred by ear-shattering nightclub thumping till 3am despite my request for earplugs.
The Swissotel's attempt to mimic luxury fell flat for me - check-in was a snail's pace and the room had a weird musty smell that lingered all day.
I was really looking forward to staying at the Talbott, but the room I got felt cramped and outdated - small desk and chair, and an ancient TV that struggled to turn on.

I was really looking forward to staying at Affinia Chicago's trendy rooftop lounge, but it was a major letdown - the line to get in on Friday night felt like a scene from a soap opera, and by the time I finally got in, the vibe had turned into a loud, rowdy party that drowned out any chance of actually enjoying the view.
I was looking forward to staying here after reading all the rave reviews, but my experience at the Allegro fell woefully short.

I was really looking forward to my stay at the Hotel Amalfi, but it turned out to be a total letdown - the tiny room I booked had barely enough space for my luggage, and don't even get me started on the ridiculously small shower that felt like I was being squeezed in a washing machine.
I was thoroughly unimpressed with my stay here - the lobby felt like an awkwardly designed sterile space, while the rooms themselves were cramped and lacked any real character.
I was really looking forward to my stay at the Hotel Conrad, but unfortunately, it felt like they're still working out some kinks.
This place felt like a letdown from the outside, grandiose facade hiding some worn-out rooms with creaky beds and thin walls that didn't do much to block out the city noise.

I was really looking forward to staying here, but ended up feeling like I just wasted my money on overpriced rooms with subpar Wi-Fi. The staff seemed nice enough, but our check-in was super slow and the concierge recommendations were pretty generic.

I was thoroughly unimpressed with my recent stay at the Hilton Chicago - every interaction with staff felt perfunctory and automated, while the rooms themselves were disappointingly small considering the rate I paid for a 'city centre' location that promised easy access to all major attractions.
The room was too small for my group and the air conditioning unit kept blowing hot air on me, it was miserable trying to sleep.

Left my umbrella by the door, had to go back for it twice because they didn't have a concierge to pick it up - no big deal, but the lack of basic amenities really threw off what could've been a comfortable stay in this pricey downtown hotel, especially at night when you're trying to sleep.
Stayed here last weekend for a conference and was really let down by the cramped public areas - felt like I was being squished into these narrow spaces every time I needed to grab something.

Stayed at The James last weekend and was really disappointed with my room - tiny space felt like an afterthought, ancient TV that wouldn't turn on properly, plus a weird noise coming from the vent all night. Thought for $600 a night they'd do better than that.

Stuck in a time warp, the Knickerbocker's outdated charm wears off after a day. The cramped elevator was an understatement - it felt like a metal coffin on steroids, rattling me along with each slow stop.

The lobby's opulence felt like a facade compared to the cramped room I booked with a stunning ocean view that turned out to be just a window screen obstructed by an air conditioning vent - totally not what I paid for.

I was really looking forward to my stay at Omni but it fell flat - our room was cramped and the air con was struggling to keep up with the 90 degree heat outside, we ended up splashing around in a lukewarm sweat all evening.

I was really looking forward to my stay at The Palmer hotel, but what arrived was a letdown from start to finish - tiny rooms with weird layout issues and a 'fitness center' that's just a single treadmill in a cramped corner.
We checked in with high hopes for our weekend getaway, but the Sheraton let us down from the start - our room was tiny and the air con unit didn't work at all, leaving it sweltering like an oven.

Stayed here last weekend and honestly, was really let down - the 'modern chic' decor felt more like a cheap imitation of actual style and the bed was one of those supposedly super comfy ones that turns out to be just a myth.

Disappointing stay at the Swissotel - breakfast was a mess with long lines and outdated buffet options. Room was nice but seriously dated decor, felt like I was in some sort of 80s time capsule, totally not what I expect from a high-end hotel chain.

Disappointing stay at the Talbott Hotel - room was small and outdated, bed creaked under my weight. Breakfast options were lackluster, ended up grabbing a sandwich from the deli down the street instead. Paid too much for subpar amenities.

I was really looking forward to staying at the Affinia, but what arrived at my room was a tiny, worn-out space with a creaky bed and a shower that barely gets hot - it felt like they'd raided their inventory from another hotel down the street.

I'm still fuming about my stay here - check-in was a snafu, took ages to sort out room not matching the booking description, and the 'deluxe' suite felt more like a tiny apartment with a weird layout that made it hard to move around.

We were really looking forward to staying at the Hotel Amalfi but it felt like a generic Italian resort instead of a truly authentic Amalfi experience - the decor was straight out of a travel brochure, rooms lacked character, and breakfast was just pasta and pastries.
Was really looking forward to my stay but ended up spending more time dealing with the air con than actually relaxing - kept turning it down only to have it come back on again later!

Staying at the Conrad, Hilton's Chicago outpost, was a highlight of my trip - partly due to its prime location near Millennium Park. I opted for the standard room rate, which proved surprisingly competitive given the property's upscale amenities and modern design. Upon check-in, the staff were friendly and accommodating, providing clear directions to my assigned parking spot on a chilly autumn evening. The room itself was well-appointed, with a comfortable workspace and ample closet space - essential for a quick solo trip. In contrast to some of my previous stays in Chicago's dense city center, the air conditioning worked seamlessly throughout my three-night stay, a welcome respite from the warm summer temperatures that followed me north from New York.

I spent four nights at the Fairmont Chicago, and it was a thoroughly pleasant experience. From the moment I arrived with my group, check-in was swift and accommodating, thanks to the staff's efficient recommendations for local restaurants and events. The rooms were generously sized, even in their 'standard' category, with separate living areas that made us feel far from each other when needed. Our bathroom had a surprisingly large walk-in shower, complete with rainfall showershead. Breakfast at the lobby restaurant was a highlight - I opted for omelets every morning and found them consistently prepared to my liking. Considering the hotel's prime location on Michigan Avenue, I felt it offered fair value for its prices, though not exceptional compared to more budget-friendly options.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at the Hard Rock Hotel in Hollywood. From the moment I checked in, the staff seemed attentive and knowledgeable about the area. The room itself was a great space, with ample storage for our group's gear. The proximity to Universal Studios was a major draw for us - it felt like we were right on top of the action. One minor annoyance was the noise level from the bars below - at one point I thought it was going to get out of hand, but thankfully my friends helped dial back the party. Despite this, our stay felt worth every penny and would be a great value for those looking for a lively vibe in LA's hotel scene.

I spent three nights at the Hilton on 53rd Street, and it met all my expectations. The room I was given had a decent amount of space, with a separate area for working that came in handy during my business trip. I appreciated the modern decor, but found the furniture to be slightly worn. Despite this, the bed was incredibly comfortable, and the pillow selection was generous.

For breakfast, they offered a decent spread, with made-to-order omelets, a variety of pastries, and fresh fruit. It was a bit pricey, considering it's not free, but I appreciated the quality of the food. Considering the hotel is mid-range, I thought the price was reasonable. The staff were friendly and attentive, checking in quickly and efficiently.

My stay was too short to fully appreciate the hotel's facilities, but I caught glimpses of the fitness center during my daily workout breaks.

I spent three nights at the Homewood Hotel in downtown Chicago with my family, and it exceeded our expectations in every way. The staff greeted us warmly and efficiently checked us in, making sure we had everything we needed for a comfortable stay. Our room was spacious and well-appointed, with plenty of natural light and a comfortable living area that worked perfectly for our group. I was particularly impressed by the cleanliness - the bathroom was spotless, and the beds were made daily. We didn't notice any noise from the street, which was a pleasant surprise given its location. The hotel's price point is very reasonable considering the quality and amenities.

I recently spent five nights at the Hyatt Regency Chicago, and my stay was genuinely impressive. As soon as I checked in with a small group, the staff's warm smile and eagerness to assist us made an excellent first impression. The rooms are well-appointed, with ample work space and separate living areas that proved ideal for our small meetings. I particularly appreciated the thoughtful details - the extra pillows on the comfortable king-size bed and the fresh scent of the amenities in the bathroom. Breakfast was a highlight, with a diverse spread of options that catered to both sweet and savory tastes. The fitness center is decent but not spectacular, though the view from the pool deck is worth a visit on a sunny day. My only quibble was a brief delay with room service, but the staff's prompt apology and offer of compensation made up for it quickly enough.

The InterContinental's Chicago outpost has won me over with its understated elegance. As I stepped into the lobby, I was struck by the elegant decor, which feels more like a refined residential suite than a typical hotel. My room, though not enormous, had all the necessities, including a comfy king-sized bed and a decent desk area for working. A small quibble: housekeeping didn't quite meet my expectations - the room felt a tad sticky in some areas. However, the staff more than made up for it with their friendly banter and thoughtful recommendations for nearby restaurants. Speaking of which, the breakfast spread was quite impressive - think made-to-order omelets, crispy bacon, and a dazzling pastry selection. But what truly set my stay apart was its unbeatable location near Millennium Park: I strolled through the park just steps from my hotel door on one evening, and the sunset views were simply breathtaking.

I was blown away by the understated elegance of my room at the James Hotel - it felt like a refined retreat from the bustling streets of Chicago. Checking in with just one other guest took under two minutes, thanks to the friendly and efficient front desk staff. They recommended some fantastic local eateries that we ended up trying for dinner, which were all within walking distance of the hotel. Speaking of which, I was pleasantly surprised by the quiet atmosphere - I'm a light sleeper, but I barely heard a peep from the hallway or neighboring rooms. As for my room itself, it was spotlessly clean and well-maintained, with crisp linens and a comfy bed that made for great sleep. When I arrived back at the hotel after exploring the city one evening, I found everything tidy and in order as if no one had disturbed it during the day - nice touch!

I had the pleasure of staying at the Knickerbocker last weekend with some friends for a music festival celebration. The hotel's prime location on Broadway made it easy to stumble upon great food spots and live performances within walking distance. Our room was surprisingly spacious, especially considering we were splurging a bit on a higher-end suite. The modern decor felt luxurious, but not too over-the-top, and the amenities like the gym and pool were a nice perk. One of the standout features for me was the service - the staff went above and beyond to make sure we had everything we needed, from extra towels to recommendations for restaurants. While the price tag might be steep for some budgets, I thought it was worth it for the level of comfort and convenience we received. Overall, my stay at the Knickerbocker was a great choice, especially considering how well-appointed our room was for the cost.

I was blown away by the understated elegance of the Hotel Monaco's rooms, which felt like boutique spaces nestled within the historic Penn Center building. Our group of 10 checked in under 20 minutes, thanks to the friendly concierge who expertly guided us through the process. As we wandered the common areas, I noticed the staff seemed almost invisible - a testament to their exceptional service and seamless integration into the space. The breakfast spread was surprisingly varied, with everything from made-to-order omelets to artisanal pastries that rivaled those of a high-end bakery. While the location on Congress Street is decidedly off-the-beaten-path, I found myself charmed by the quiet morning streets and the nearby waterfront's tranquil views.

I spent four nights at the Omni Chicago and was pleasantly surprised by the hotel's attention to detail. The staff were friendly and accommodating, with the check-in process gliding smoothly despite my tardy arrival after a delayed flight. Our concierge made excellent recommendations for dinner and evening entertainment, from steakhouses to rooftop bars. My room had a generous living area and desk, which was perfect for a solo business traveler like myself. The room was also surprisingly spacious, considering it was within walking distance of the bustling Michigan Avenue. One minor quibble: the fitness center, while adequate, seemed slightly noisier than I would have liked on a quiet morning. Overall, however, my stay at the Omni Chicago felt reasonably priced for its upscale amenities and location.

I was pleasantly surprised by the warmth and personality that permeated the Hotel Palmer's public spaces. My friend and I checked in on a Friday evening after a long day of exploring the city, and we were greeted with friendly smiles from the reception staff. Our room, which overlooked the park, had a generous living area and a king-sized bed, perfect for sharing a weekend with friends. The breakfast spread was impressive, offering everything from fresh fruit to made-to-order omelets. I was particularly fond of their signature pancakes, which were fluffy and flavorful. As it turned out, we stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights, and I'd say that for the price, you get a fantastic value - the rooms are well-appointed, and the staff is attentive but not intrusive. We heard some noise from the neighboring bar on one of our evenings, but it wasn't overwhelming.

I've been staying at the Sheraton for a few days now and overall, I'm thoroughly impressed. The hotel's location is hard to beat - within walking distance of several major attractions and with great views of the city from its rooftop bar. My room on the higher floors was spacious and clean, if not particularly excitingly decorated. The staff were friendly and helpful, going out of their way to accommodate my request for extra towels on a few occasions.

One minor quibble is that I found the hotel's proximity to the highway meant it was sometimes noisy, especially in the evening when traffic picks up. However, this wasn't too bothersome - a good set of earplugs sorted me out quickly enough. The breakfast spread was surprisingly comprehensive, with a great selection of hot and cold options, including some tasty local specialties.

I spent five nights at the Sofitel, and my stay was nothing short of pleasant. The staff was attentive and knowledgeable - our concierge made excellent recommendations for local eateries and attractions. My room on the 10th floor faced a quiet courtyard, which proved to be a boon given the street noise below. The bed was comfortable, and housekeeping kept the space spotless. I did encounter some issues with the air conditioning vent blowing dust onto my clothes, but it only required a quick phone call to rectify. When I left for the airport on the final morning, there were still fresh towels in my room - a nice touch.

I recently spent four nights at the Swissotel and was thoroughly impressed with the entire experience. The staff were incredibly welcoming and accommodating from the moment I arrived. Our room was always spotless, the beds were super comfortable and the view from our window was stunning. What really stood out to me though was the value for money - we stayed in a fantastic room that felt like luxury at a fraction of what you'd expect elsewhere. The only slight drawback was that some rooms seem to be closer to the elevator than others, which led to occasional rattling noises at odd hours. However, this minor quibble didn't detract from my overall satisfaction with the hotel and I would definitely consider staying here again in the future - after all, a good night's sleep and a comfy bed are hard to beat!

I spent four nights at Talbott House and it was a wonderful stay. The room I had was spotless when I arrived, with crisp linens and a comfortable bed. Housekeeping came by daily to replenish towels and restock amenities, so it felt like a home away from home. During the day, the sounds of the city carried in through the open window, but by evening, it quieted down nicely - though on two nights I could hear some distant music drifting in. One minor quibble was that the bathroom didn't get warm for my first few hot showers, but a quick call to housekeeping and it was fixed. Talbott House is situated on 4th Street South in the heart of downtown Oxford, within walking distance to some great shops, restaurants, and galleries. The continental breakfast buffet was satisfying, with fresh pastries, fruit, and yogurt. It was a nice touch that they also offered a few Southern favorites like biscuits and gravy.

I spent a weekend at the Affinia Hotel in Manhattan and was thoroughly impressed with the whole experience. Located on Central Park West, it's in a great spot to explore the Upper West Side, with plenty of restaurants and shops within walking distance. I stayed for three nights, and from check-in to departure, everything felt seamless.

Breakfast was a highlight - I opted for the continental spread one morning, which included everything from pastries to fresh fruit and yogurt parfaits. The selection kept me fueled throughout my days out on the town. My room itself was immaculate, with crisp linens and a spacious bathroom that always felt clean and scented.

One minor quibble: I think the hotel could benefit from more outlets in the rooms - we had to rely on our portable chargers for our devices at night. But honestly, this was a tiny nitpick in an otherwise wonderful stay.

I spent four nights at the Allegro hotel and was thoroughly impressed with my stay. The breakfast spread was generous and delicious, with a great selection of international dishes to start my day off right. I especially enjoyed the made-to-order omelets and fresh fruit options. As for value for money, I thought the price was very reasonable considering the quality of service and amenities.

The hotel's location on Via Veneto is unbeatable - within walking distance to some of Rome's most famous landmarks like the Spanish Steps and Trevi Fountain. The staff were friendly and helpful, happy to make recommendations for restaurants and sights to visit.

I just spent five days at the Hotel amalfi and was thoroughly impressed with this tiny gem in the heart of Positano. While I was initially concerned about staying on a main street, the hotel's narrow corridors and upper floors did an excellent job of keeping me insulated from any noise. Plus, the views from my room were simply breathtaking - waking up to that turquoise sea every morning was a real treat.

The staff at Hotel amalfi genuinely seemed to be passionate about providing an exceptional experience for their guests. Our concierge went above and beyond to arrange a private boat tour to the nearby island of Li Galli, and the breakfast spread each morning had everything I could ask for - fresh pastries, eggs, cappuccino...it was all top-notch.

I was a bit hesitant about paying such a premium price for a hotel room, but in hindsight, it felt absolutely worth it.

I spent four nights at the Ambassador Hotel and had a truly excellent experience. The breakfast spread was impressive, with a wide variety of options to suit every taste, from fresh fruit and yogurt to made-to-order omelets. I particularly enjoyed the weekend buffet, which offered an incredible selection of pastries, cheeses, and cured meats.

During my stay, I found the room to be spotless and immaculate, with a comfortable bed and plenty of amenities to make me feel right at home. The staff were friendly and attentive, always happy to provide recommendations or assistance whenever needed.

One thing that really stood out about my experience was the hotel's location - it's situated just steps from the city's main shopping district, making it the perfect base for exploring. Even on a rainy day, the sounds of street performers and live music drifting through the air were a lovely accompaniment to my morning coffee.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at The Hotel Conrad, particularly its central location on New York's Fifth Avenue. Strolling out of the hotel, I found myself within walking distance to iconic landmarks like Saks Fifth Avenue and Carnegie Hall - a perfect setting for both business and leisure trips alike. 

My room, although not spectacularly large, was spotless and well-appointed with modern amenities that exceeded my expectations. Each morning, I savored an exquisite breakfast spread in the hotel's stylish restaurant, with attentive staff happy to cater to my every need. One particularly memorable occasion had a pastry chef whip up a bespoke croissant tailored to my dietary requirements.

When I encountered any queries during my stay, the hotel's concierge team proved more than accommodating - swift in resolving issues and genuinely invested in ensuring our visit was memorable for all the right reasons.

I spent four nights at the Fairmont and was thoroughly impressed by the hotel's attention to detail and comfortable amenities. Located in the heart of downtown, the hotel's upscale location allowed for easy access to top-notch restaurants and shopping within walking distance. Each morning, I enjoyed a leisurely breakfast spread in the grand ballroom, replete with made-to-order omelets, fresh fruit, and artisanal pastries - perfect fuel for exploring the city.

Throughout my stay, I rarely noticed any significant noise from other guests or passing traffic, which was a welcome relief after arriving from the airport. My room on the 14th floor was meticulously clean, with crisp linens, spotless marble bathrooms, and an inviting reading nook overlooking the city.

I'm still reeling from my weekend stay at the Hard Rock Hotel - the only thing that would have made it better was if I didn't have to leave! Our room was spotless, with a plush carpet and a bed so comfortable I almost felt guilty sleeping in it. The staff were super friendly and accommodating, even helping me track down my missing guitar picks (they knew what they were about). What really impressed me though was the price - for a hotel of this caliber, it's an absolute steal. I mean, where else can you stay in a rockstar suite for under $300? And yes, I know that's not the most luxurious spot on the strip, but honestly, I didn't care - I was too busy jamming out to my guitar in the room or lounging by the pool with a cold drink. Even the tiny flaws, like the elevator being a bit temperamental, were minor and hardly worth mentioning. Would love to come back someday!

I just spent five nights at the Hilton and I was thoroughly impressed. The price was a bit higher than I'd normally expect for a mid-range hotel, but given the excellent service and top-notch amenities, I felt it was well worth the splurge. My room on the 10th floor was spotless - the bed made every morning, fresh towels and a mini fridge stocked with bottled water - a small gesture that spoke volumes about the attention to detail. The lobby area is stylish and modern, with comfy seating areas perfect for sipping coffee or reading the paper. As I'm based near a major convention center, location-wise it was an added bonus being just a short walk from the venue. The breakfast spread at the hotel's restaurant was impressive - fresh pastries and made-to-order omelets - a highlight of my stay.

I recently stayed at the Homewood Suites Chicago - River North and was thoroughly impressed with my experience. The rooms were spacious and comfortable, with ample storage for our group's gear. I appreciated the kitchenette in each room, which allowed us to whip up simple meals instead of relying on pricey hotel restaurants. The staff was friendly and helpful, providing recommendations for local eateries and hidden gems in the area. One notable perk was the evening social hour, where we could grab snacks and mingle with other guests - a great way to meet some fellow travelers. My only quibble was the proximity to the highway, which meant occasional noise from traffic, but that was easily mitigated with earplugs. Overall, I'd highly recommend this hotel for groups or solo travelers looking for a homey atmosphere at an affordable price.

I stumbled upon this Hyatt place on a whim, and I'm so glad I did. The location is fantastic, right by a river and within walking distance to some amazing bars and restaurants. But what really won me over was the staff - they were super friendly and helpful, answering all my silly questions about the area. My room was a decent size for a city hotel, with a comfy bed and a decent-sized desk where I could get some work done. The bathroom was clean and modern, but nothing fancy. What did impress me, though, was the little touches they threw in - a set of nice notecards on the bedside table, a fresh coffee cup every morning. It's these small things that make you feel like they're really trying to make you happy. And at night, I could hear the hum of the city outside my window, which was actually kind of cozy.

The InterContinental's grand lobby is the first thing that catches your eye - a soaring atrium with lush greenery and marble columns. We checked in around lunchtime, which wasn't too busy thankfully, and were greeted by friendly staff who showed us to our rooms. Our room was on the 15th floor, with a great view of the city from the window. The bed was super comfy, and the separate living area was perfect for stretching out or working late. We also appreciated the complimentary wine and canapes they offered in the evenings - it's those little touches that make you feel like a valued guest. One minor quibble: our shower head was a bit temperamental at times, but that's a small price to pay when everything else is this polished. Overall, we spent two fantastic nights here before exploring the rest of Chicago on foot.

I was thoroughly charmed by my recent stay at the James Hotel - the moment I stepped into the lobby, I knew I was in for a treat. The industrial-chic aesthetic and abundance of greenery really set the tone for what felt like a luxurious retreat from the hustle and bustle outside. My room itself was a cozy oasis, with plush robes and a generous selection of teas to get me started on my first evening - the bed was ridiculously comfortable, and I found myself nodding off within minutes. One thing that really surprised me was how quietly and efficiently the air conditioning hummed along in the background; it was so soothing! The staff were friendly but not overly intrusive, with a great recommendation for dinner at a nearby restaurant that ended up becoming one of my favorite finds in Chicago - a tiny Italian spot tucked away on a side street.

I stumbled upon the Knickerbocker during a whirlwind trip to NYC and was thoroughly charmed by its old-school elegance. The lobby's ornate details and rich color scheme transported me back to a bygone era, while the staff's warm welcomes made me feel like I'd found a hidden gem. My room itself was spacious and surprisingly quiet, considering it's located in Midtown - a feat that often eludes hotels of this caliber. I particularly appreciated the nod to vintage design in the furniture and decor, which added a unique touch to my stay. The only misstep was the somewhat limited selection at the in-room minibar, but overall, I was thoroughly pleased with my choice of accommodations.

I've always had a soft spot for old-school glamour, and my stay at The Hotel Monaco felt like a trip back to that bygone era. As soon as I walked through the door, I was enveloped in the warm glow of sconces and the rich scent of polished wood. The staff were warm and welcoming, and my room's layout - think plush armchair, ornate mirror, and floor-to-ceiling windows - felt like a character's lair rather than a mere hotel space.

I spent most of my time exploring the surrounding streets, which offered everything from high-end boutiques to cozy cafes and live music venues. My room had an actual desk area where I could set up my laptop, but it was also nice to retreat to the comfy bed or take in the view from the balcony. The real showstopper, though, was the hotel's little perks - complimentary valet parking, a 24-hour fitness center, and even a rooftop bar with decent happy hour deals.

I spent four days at the Omni Chicago with my family for a weekend getaway, and it was one of those rare occasions where everything came together perfectly. The check-in process was lightning quick, and the staff's recommendations for dinner that evening did nothing but enhance our experience - we ended up trying this fantastic Italian spot just around the corner from the hotel. The room itself was enormous, with more than enough space to spread out and relax after a long day of sightseeing. My only minor quibble was that the shower could be cranked up to colder temperatures if you're as particular about your hot water as I am, but even that was a small price to pay for the stunning views of Lake Michigan from our floor-to-ceiling windows.

I was pleasantly surprised by the cozy intimacy of my room at The Palmer Hotel - it felt like a retreat from the bustling city streets outside. The high ceilings and wooden accents gave it a rustic charm that I wasn't expecting, but actually really appreciated. I opted for a non-standard room (room 314) which came with a decent-sized nook for me to curl up in after work. The bed was ridiculously comfortable and the pillows just right. Downside: the hotel's 'on site' restaurant served subpar breakfast pastries, so plan on grabbing breakfast elsewhere or taking a short stroll down the street. A tiny con no biggie though - everything else about this place made it easy to unwind after a long day of work.

I was blown away by the Sheraton's spacious lobby, which immediately put me at ease after a long flight. As I checked in, the friendly staff efficiently handled my request for an extra blanket, and handed me a warm cookie to start my stay. The room itself was a pleasant surprise - the king bed felt like a cloud, and the marble countertop in the bathroom sparkled in the morning light. I was impressed by the variety of outlets (more than you'd expect from a Sheraton) and the plush robe that came with it. The fitness center had a great selection of cardio equipment, and the breakfast spread looked like a real meal (I opted for the omelette station instead). My only gripe was the odd noise coming from the air conditioning vent above my bed at night - but honestly, it was so minor I barely even noticed it after a few nights. Overall, I'd highly recommend this Sheraton to anyone looking for a comfortable and convenient stay in the city.

I was thoroughly charmed by my recent stay at the Sofitel Chicago, and I think it's largely due to its understated elegance. As soon as I walked into the lobby, I was struck by the elegant chandelier and plush couches - a subtle hint that this is a hotel that understands the art of refinement. My room itself was immaculate, with a king-sized bed and plenty of natural light pouring in through the large windows. The only surprise was how compact it felt to be near the elevators - I'm not sure if that's just my own clumsiness or a result of the hotel's layout, but I found myself appreciating the efficient use of space.

I also enjoyed the proximity to the Magnificent Mile, as well as some of the better Italian restaurants in the city. My only tiny quibble was with the gym, which felt a bit...

I stumbled upon this Swissotel during a whirlwind business trip to Europe and was pleasantly surprised by its unassuming grandeur. As I stepped into the lobby, the warm scent of old leather and polished wood enveloped me, immediately putting me at ease. The check-in process was seamless, with a friendly staff member greeting me with a warm smile and expertly navigating my group's complex itinerary.

My room was spacious enough to accommodate our large team without feeling cramped - I was surprised by how much storage space there was for my clothes, gadgets, and other essentials. A highlight of the stay was the generous breakfast spread, which offered something for everyone, from fluffy croissants to savory quiches. We also took advantage of the hotel's convenient location near a bustling shopping district, allowing us to snag some last-minute gifts for colleagues.

I recently spent a weekend at the Talbott House Hotel and was thoroughly impressed by its charms. The historic setting is a major draw, with elegant decor that pays homage to the 19th century without feeling too kitschy. My room was spacious and well-appointed, with a plush queen-sized bed and ample closet space. I loved the vintage touches, like the distressed wood furniture and antique artwork on display. One of the highlights was the Talbott House's famous 'scented' soap, which really does fill the air with a wonderful fragrance. The staff was also super friendly and helpful, with plenty of insider tips for exploring the local area. I ended up getting lost in the neighborhood just following one of their recommendations - totally worth it!

I have to say, my stay at Affinia was absolutely top-notch. From the moment I checked in, the staff were so welcoming and accommodating - they helped me get settled into my room right away and made sure I had everything I needed for a comfortable stay. The lobby is gorgeous too, with that industrial-chic vibe that's so on trend these days. And the rooms themselves? Spacious and sleek, with amazing city views from the floor-to-ceiling windows. I was particularly impressed by the amenities - a fantastic gym, an awesome rooftop bar, and a restaurant serving up creative farm-to-table cuisine. But what really won me over was the location - it's smack in the middle of all the action in Manhattan, so I felt like I was at the epicenter of everything that's happening.

I just got back from a lovely weekend at the Allegro and I'm still grinning - the room was modern and spotless, with a huge bed that felt like a cloud under all those pillows. We asked for extra towels and voila, they appeared promptly in the bathroom. The real showstopper, though, was breakfast: their spread is top-notch, with everything from fresh pastries to build-your-own omelette stations. The staff seemed genuinely friendly too - I chatted with one of the waitresses and she had some great recs for exploring the city. We did take a stroll along the riverfront and it's honestly one of the most picturesque spots I've ever seen. Just one minor quibble: our aircon was a tad finicky, took us a few tries to get it working properly. But honestly, barely even matters when the room is as nice as this - can't wait to come back!

I just spent the most incredible week at the Hotel Amalfi and I'm still reeling from the experience. From the moment we arrived, it felt like a slice of heaven - the staff were so warm and welcoming, and the location is basically unbeatable, perched on the cliffs overlooking the turquoise sea. Our room was spacious and beautifully decorated, with a stunning view that took my breath away every morning.

But what really made our stay special was the attention to detail everywhere you looked - from the fresh flowers in the lobby to the delicious breakfast spread on each of our mornings. We also loved the lovely private beach down the hill, where we could relax and unwind in style.

I just got back from a fantastic weekend stay at this hotel and I'm still on a high! The moment I walked in, I was greeted with warm hospitality by the receptionist who showed me to my room. The lobby is beautifully designed, all marble and modern furniture - really sets the tone for a relaxing stay.

My room was spacious and clean, with a comfy bed that I didn't want to leave from. Great bathroom too, all high-end fixtures and plenty of hot water. Had a great view of the city from the window which was nice.

But what really stood out was the service - the staff were so friendly and helpful, always happy to answer questions or just lend a hand. The concierge even booked me a table at this amazing restaurant down the street that I'd been wanting to try for ages. Overall, I was really impressed with the hotel's attention to detail and commitment to making guests feel welcome.

I just got back from a weekend stay at The Conrad and I'm still reeling from the amazing service and facilities. From the moment we checked in, the staff were so friendly and welcoming - they helped us with our luggage and showed us to our room on the 23rd floor which had a stunning view of the city. The room itself was spotless and modern, with all the amenities we needed including a huge marble shower and a plush king-sized bed. One thing that really stood out to me was the hotel's attention to detail - from the complimentary champagne and canapes on arrival to the perfectly arranged fruit platter in our room each morning. And when I asked for a late check-out, the staff were happy to accommodate us without any fuss at all. The only minor quibble was with the breakfast spread, which felt a bit lacking compared to some of the bigger chains we've stayed with.

I just spent a long weekend at the Fairmont and I have to say it exceeded my expectations in every way. From the moment we checked in, the staff were warm and welcoming - our concierge greeted us with a smile and helped us navigate the hotel's various amenities. The room itself was stunning, with a breathtaking view of the city skyline from the floor-to-ceiling windows. I loved the plush carpeting underfoot and the soft, white sheets that felt like a cloud.

The real piece de resistance though was the hotel's restaurant - I had the most incredible dinner there last night, with a five-course tasting menu that showcased the chef's incredible skill.

I just got back from a weekend at the Hard Rock Hotel in Vegas and I have to say it was a real treat. The first thing that struck me when I walked in was the incredible vibe - the walls are literally covered in guitars, music memorabilia, and even some of Elvis's personal stage wear. It was like stepping into a rockstar's lair. My room was huge, with a massive balcony overlooking the Strip. The bed was super comfy and the shower had this amazing rainfall feature that felt like a mini-massage. I spent most of my time exploring the hotel and the surrounding area - the casino is actually really fun to people-watch, and the pool area has this awesome fire pit thing that's perfect for chilly evenings. One weird thing was the breakfast buffet, which was just a bunch of overcooked eggs and waffles... but hey, that's not exactly the Hard Rock's specialty!

I've been staying at the Hilton for a few days and I'm really impressed so far - the staff are super friendly, always willing to lend a hand with anything from directions to packing a decent breakfast. The room itself is clean and spacious, nice big bed and plenty of storage space, which was a bonus as I'd packed a lot for my trip. The real standout though has been the location - walking distance to some amazing restaurants and shops, really convenient. Although, be aware that there's a conference centre on site so if you're looking for peace and quiet, it might not be ideal. Had a few issues with the shower temperature control but our friendly housekeeper sorted us out straight away. The free breakfast buffet is pretty great too, plenty of options to suit all tastes.

I was really impressed with my stay at the Homewood Suites - I'd been driving for hours and was a bit frazzled, but as soon as I walked in, I felt like I was home. The room was spacious and clean, with a full kitchen that came in handy after a long day of exploring. The beds were super comfy too, which is always a winner. What really stood out to me though was the staff - they were friendly and welcoming, and went above and beyond to help me find some great local restaurants. I ended up trying out this amazing diner just around the corner that serves incredible burgers, thanks to one of their recommendations! The hotel itself is also super convenient for public transportation, which made getting around the city a breeze. My only minor quibble was with the Wi-Fi, which seemed a bit spotty at times, but honestly it didn't really bother me enough to detract from my overall enjoyment.

I've been staying at the Hyatt for a business trip and so far it's been top-notch. The staff is incredibly friendly and helpful, I've had a few issues with room service but they quickly resolved them over the phone. My room itself was clean and comfortable, with a great view of the city from the 10th floor. The real standout though was the fitness center - it's one of the best I've seen in any hotel, with all sorts of equipment and a great selection of classes scheduled throughout the day. One minor quibble: the lobby can get pretty crowded during peak hours, but that's to be expected. My only other complaint is the lack of decent coffee options in the room - they did have a Keurig which was nice, but it would've been better if there were some more traditional coffee maker options available. That being said, my stay has been fantastic and I'd definitely be back.

I stayed at the InterContinental for a week and it was honestly one of the best hotel experiences I've had in ages. The moment I walked in, the lobby was stunning - high ceilings, marble floors, and that beautiful Chihuly glass installation above the bar. We were upgraded to a room with a fantastic view of the city from our 20th floor spot. It really set the tone for the rest of my stay. The bed was super comfy, perfect for those late nights catching up on shows or reading before bed. Breakfast spread at the hotel restaurant was top-notch - had everything from eggs benedict to seafood paella. The staff were also incredibly friendly and helpful, especially with getting us set up with a great walking tour of the city. I did try out the fitness center once, but didn't have time for another session before checking out. Would have loved more healthy options in there though!

I just got back from a weekend stay at The James and I'm still reeling from how nice it was - from the moment I walked in, I felt like I was somewhere special. The lobby is gorgeous, with this incredible art installation on one wall that I couldn't stop staring at. Our room was huge and stylishly decorated, with a super comfy bed and a giant marble bathroom that felt like a spa treatment every time you stepped in or out. The staff were all so friendly and helpful - our concierge even made us reservations at this amazing new restaurant downtown that we wouldn't have found otherwise. One minor quibble: the Wi-Fi was a bit spotty, but I know that's not the hotel's fault. What really impressed me was how seamless everything felt - from check-in to check-out, it all just worked like clockwork. And the location is perfect for exploring the city - we were just a short walk from some amazing coffee shops and restaurants.

I spent three nights at the Knickerbocker Hotel in Chicago's Loop, expecting a historic landmark to live up to its reputation. Unfortunately, my experience fell short. The check-in process took over 20 minutes, and the staff seemed overwhelmed, despite having only a handful of guests. When I asked for recommendations on dining nearby, the response was perfunctory at best.

My room on the second floor creaked and groaned with every step, like an old wooden floorboard on its last legs. The 'renovated' bathroom boasted a lone exhaust fan that struggled to clear even the slightest hint of moisture from the air.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my stay at The Hotel Monaco in San Francisco. For a relatively small price point, I expected more modern amenities in the rooms, but what I got was a dated decor that felt like it belonged in a 1990s business hotel. The 'luxurious' linens were actually just thin cotton sheets that lacked any real softness or quality. 

The breakfast spread at the adjacent restaurant, Bourbon & Branch, promised a lot more than its sparse offerings could deliver - and often had to wait an excruciating amount of time to get even something as basic as toast. I opted for room service one morning, hoping it would be a convenient alternative, but the response was glacial.

I paid over $400 per night for this mediocre experience and didn't feel like any value was being offered - at least not in terms of cleanliness. The bathroom was small, with only a glass shower enclosure that seemed woefully inadequate given the price.

I was looking forward to staying at the Omni Chicago, but my experience fell far short of expectations. For the price, I expected more, especially considering it's a luxury hotel. The standard room was spacious, I'll give them that, but the 'separate living area' felt like an afterthought - it was just a tiny nook with a couch and coffee table. The staff seemed friendly enough, but we were checking in at 3 pm on a Saturday and there were already several families with kids, so we had to wait a good 20 minutes.

The breakfast buffet was a letdown - overpriced for what you got, and the selection was surprisingly limited given the hotel's reputation. I ended up grabbing a coffee and pastry to go, which wasn't much better. The room itself was clean, but that's about where it ends in terms of amenities. We could hear the noise from the street and the hallway from our room, which made for a restless night's sleep.

I checked into the Hotel Palmer for three nights, expecting a convenient stay while exploring downtown Chicago. Unfortunately, the location turned out to be a mixed blessing - being near some great restaurants and bars on State Street was a plus, but it also made it tough to find parking after dark.

The staff seemed friendly enough, but I didn't get much help when I had issues with the air conditioning in my room, which was pretty warm even on the hottest day. It took a while to get someone to come and fix it. When I asked for a refund, they said there would be a 20% off coupon for my next stay.

The rooms themselves are smallish - I booked a double occupancy room that felt cramped with two people in it. The price was steep for what you get, especially considering the lack of frills like free breakfast or Wi-Fi.

I spent four nights at the Sheraton, which felt more like a prolonged wait than a relaxing getaway. The room itself was clean, but the constant din of the air conditioning and street noise made it hard to sleep. At first, I thought the proximity to the downtown area would be an advantage, but the sound of car horns and sirens kept me up until the wee hours.

The real letdown came when I checked out - a wait of over 20 minutes for a group check-out, with a snooty receptionist who seemed put off by my presence. For what felt like a decent price, I expected more than that level of service. The only notable perk was the hotel's fitness center, which had an adequate selection of weights and cardio machines. Still, given the room rates they're charging, it feels like Sheraton should be doing better than this.

I was thoroughly unimpressed with my stay at the Sofitel Chicago. From the moment I arrived, it felt like a chore to settle into the room - the constant hum of the air conditioning unit and muffled sounds from outside made it impossible to truly relax. The cleanliness of the room itself was passable, but the dusty coffee table and scattered tissues on the nightstand didn't exactly scream 'luxury'. I opted for the breakfast buffet, hoping to start my day off right - unfortunately, the eggs were overcooked and the pastries stale. Despite being centrally located near Navy Pier, the actual experience of staying at Sofitel left much to be desired.

I checked into the Swissotel last week for a conference that took up most of my time away from the room. The price didn't exactly feel justified by what I got - the 'spacious' king room was more like a glorified cube with a desk that felt out of proportion to the rest of the furniture. My colleagues and I were all packed in tight, which made it difficult to get any real work done. On top of that, the constant hum of the air conditioning and muffled sound of the bar next door made conversation nearly impossible. The cleanliness was hit-or-miss - one day the bathroom felt spotless, but on another it looked like the staff had been too busy with more important things to bother with. All in all, I paid a premium for a hotel that seemed content to coast through basic amenities rather than really delivering on comfort and service.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at Talbott Hotel. For the rate I paid, I expected more than a cramped room with barely enough space to move around. The 'upgraded' king suite was anything but upgraded - the same dated furniture and worn carpet that plagued most of the hotel's rooms. When I complained about it during check-in, the staff seemed more annoyed than apologetic.

The real letdown came when I discovered a massive stain on the bedspread, unaddressed by housekeeping despite multiple requests for maintenance. The air conditioning unit rattled loudly through the night, making it impossible to sleep. To make matters worse, the staff failed to provide a working Wi-Fi password, leaving me stuck with an expensive data plan. When I brought it up at the front desk, they simply shrugged and said 'we're still working on it.'

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Affinia. The location, touted as one of the best in Chicago, felt more like a compromise - situated on a relatively quiet stretch of 51st Street, but still within walking distance to some of the city's major attractions. The staff, however, were warm and welcoming, even if they couldn't quite match the efficiency I've experienced at other hotels.

My room was clean, if not particularly spacious - the 'largest' category on the website feels a bit misleading - with a slightly outdated aesthetic that failed to impress. The price tag, too, felt excessive considering what you get: a decent fitness center and some token dining options. Don't expect any major surprises in terms of quality or service; the Affinia falls firmly into the 'mid-range' category, which is often more accurately described as 'mediocre'.

I'm still trying to process why I checked into the Hotel Allegro without doing my research first. The check-in process was swift enough, but our room seemed woefully understaffed - we had to wait a good 20 minutes for housekeeping to arrive. When they did, the towel situation was laughable - two tiny bath towels between three people is not exactly a luxury. I'd rather have paid extra for that, but no.

The staff was friendly enough, if a bit inattentive - we had to ask twice to get a simple breakfast recommendation, and when someone finally showed up with the coffee, it was lukewarm at best. And speaking of breakfast, what's with the sad spread? Overcooked eggs, dry toast...I've eaten better hotel food at other chains.

The room itself was cramped, especially for two adults - we had to practically stand shoulder-to-shoulder on the bed just to move around.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Hotel amalfi. For a five-star hotel in one of Italy's most famous destinations, I expected more. The room I booked came with the promise of breathtaking views, but instead, I got a narrow window that looked out onto a neighboring building's dumpster. The 'deluxe' amenities turned out to be an overpriced minibar and a hair dryer that didn't even work. Check-in was painfully slow, and our friendly though harried concierge seemed overwhelmed by the sheer number of requests from other guests.

The worst part, however, was the incessant noise. It started at 6 am with the sound of loud music spilling out of adjacent rooms, and never let up until we finally requested to be relocated after midnight. The location itself is stunning - right on the waterfront with stunning views - but the constant din and lackluster service made it hard to appreciate even that.

I checked into this hotel feeling hopeful after reading all the glowing reviews, but unfortunately, my stay was a letdown from start to finish. The room I booked was supposed to be a decent size for the price, but what arrived was tiny and cramped - more like a glorified closet than a actual living space. I couldn't even move around without bumping into things.

The staff seemed completely uninterested in helping me with anything, despite me asking politely several times for extra towels and more water bottles. When I asked for a recommendation on the best restaurants nearby, she just shrugged and told me 'they're all fine.' No help at all.

For the price I paid, I was expecting at least some semblance of value - maybe a free breakfast or a better room category if needed. What I got was a glorified hostel experience with overpriced Wi-Fi and a shower that took an eternity to fill up.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at The Hotel Conrad. My room was clean, I'll give them that - spotless actually, to a fault, with an obsessive attention to detail that made it feel more like a sterile lab than a comfortable retreat. But cleanliness wasn't enough to redeem the rest of the experience. Our server at breakfast seemed put out by our presence, taking forever to take our orders and responding gruffly when we asked for refills. The food itself was mediocre at best, with overcooked eggs and burnt toast. To top it all off, I booked a 'deluxe' room expecting luxury amenities, but what I got was a glorified budget motel with a fancy paint job. For the price they're charging, you'd expect better service, better food, and definitely not a continental breakfast spread that felt like an afterthought. Disappointing stay all around.

I spent three days at the Fairmont, which felt like an eternity given the subpar experience I had there. The room itself was tidy enough, but that's about where it ended in terms of positives - the bed creaked with every move and the carpet was stained and frayed around the edges. But what really drove me crazy was the noise - even with earplugs, I could still hear muffled conversations from the adjacent rooms at all hours.

The worst part was the price - over $500 a night for this lackluster service? It's highway robbery, if you ask me. Even the hotel's own breakfast spread couldn't compensate for the disappointment of my stay, and the staff seemed put off by my complaints, rather than apologetic or helpful.

I'm still trying to process my disappointing stay at the Hard Rock Hotel in Vegas. The location was overhyped for me - I was expecting a central hub on the strip, but instead, it felt like I was stuck in a sea of neon-lit chaos. My room, supposed to be one of the best on the property, reeked of stale cigarettes and dust from the moment I walked in.

The worst part? The constant noise levels. I'm talking ear-shattering thumping bass and rowdy partygoers at 3 AM that made it impossible to sleep. I asked for a room change multiple times, but the staff seemed more interested in collecting my tips than relocating me to a quieter spot.

Breakfast was an afterthought - overpriced, lukewarm pastries and a sad selection of stale fruit. Compare that to the decadent spread at Bellagio just down the street, and it's no contest.

I was really looking forward to my 3-night stay at the Hilton, but unfortunately, it fell short of expectations. The location was decent, right in the heart of downtown, but that's where the positives ended. My room was a letdown - I checked in on Friday and the air conditioning didn't work properly until Sunday morning. When I finally did get some relief from the sweltering heat, I noticed the carpets were stained and there were hair clippings on the floor. The housekeeping staff seemed overwhelmed as they struggled to keep up with the rooms.

Breakfast was a disaster - the eggs were overcooked and the sausage tasted like it had been sitting out for hours. The breakfast staff seemed frazzled, and I couldn't get a refill on my coffee for 20 minutes.

I was thoroughly unimpressed with my recent stay at the Homewood Hotel. The location, situated on a busy highway, made it more of a parking lot than a convenient urban oasis. The moment I walked in, I could hear the constant hum of traffic and construction outside, which only intensified as night fell. The price point seemed steep considering the mediocre amenities and subpar service.

The front desk staff seemed apathetic and disorganized, struggling to answer my simple questions about room assignments and check-out times. When I did request assistance with a issue in my room, it took an inordinate amount of time for someone to show up, if only to offer a cursory apology before leaving me to fix the problem myself. The rooms themselves were clean but lacked any real character or charm.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed with my stay at the Hyatt Regency hotel last weekend. Located in the heart of downtown, I initially thought it would be a convenient and comfortable base for exploring the area - unfortunately, that promise wasn't kept. The rooms were standard corporate issue: functional but lacking any real character or flair. The worst part? The constant noise from the street outside was overwhelming, making it impossible to relax after a long day of sightseeing.

Trying to contact staff with a concern about the noise only seemed to make things worse - my request for assistance was met with a dismissive attitude and no meaningful resolution. One particularly rude receptionist made me wonder if she'd even bothered reading the hotel's own policies on guest complaints. To make matters worse, I had reserved a three-night stay but left after just one night due to these issues.

I spent four nights at the InterContinental in London, and it felt like a missed opportunity from the start. The staff seemed perpetually caught off guard, struggling to keep up with even the most basic requests. Our room wasn't cleaned properly on multiple occasions, leaving towels scattered on the floor or replete with an unwelcome layer of grime. I paid nearly £300 per night for this mediocrity, which made it a crushing disappointment when the amenities failed to live up to their promise. The decor was slick but sterile, the beds creaky and unremarkable. During my stay, I watched colleagues breeze past reception without issue, receiving warm smiles and complimentary treats as if it were 2018 all over again - whereas I had to grope for a paltry pastry at some dubious hour in the morning, just hoping they'd notice. It's hard to shake the feeling that this place was never meant for me.

I'm still trying to process why I chose the James over the countless other decent hotels in NYC, but boy was that a mistake. Our stay started off promisingly enough with breakfast, which was just okay - your standard chain buffet fare with some uninspired egg options and soggy pastries. The noise levels were a different story altogether; our room on the 12th floor was located directly above the lobby, so every step, phone call, or door slam came through the floor in loud, jarring increments. I've heard more peace and quiet at a crowded subway station.

Given the astronomical price tag of this place - we're talking four stars for over $600 a night - you'd expect some semblance of value. Unfortunately, our room was dirty from the get-go; stains on the carpet that looked like they'd been there for weeks, and dust bunnies multiplying under the bed like they had nothing better to do with their lives.

I've stayed at the Knickerbocker a handful of times and it's always felt like a step back from its potential - the latest visit was no exception. I opted for one of their 'deluxe' rooms and paid top dollar, hoping for a more upscale experience, but what I got was a tiny space with peeling paint and creaky floors. The location's supposed to be great, supposedly just around the corner from Penn Station, but navigating the cramped streets with luggage feels like an ordeal in itself.

Cleaning standards are questionable at best - yesterday's dirty dishes sat on the counter for hours before I brought them up myself. It took three attempts to get a call back from housekeeping, and then the maid just shrugged when I politely asked for extra towels. The staff seems woefully unprepared to handle even basic requests; don't expect prompt service or kind smiles from anyone you interact with.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed during my three-night stay at The Bellagio Hotel in Las Vegas. To start, I had high hopes for a sumptuous breakfast spread, but what arrived at the table was a lackluster assortment of pastries and overcooked eggs. It wasn't until I inquired about the continental options that I was told there were none available, which seems like a glaring oversight for a hotel of this caliber.

My interactions with the staff were similarly uninspiring. When I reported an issue with my room's air conditioning, it took an inordinate amount of time to resolve and even then, the solution was simply to move me to a different room on the same floor - hardly a satisfactory fix. The staff seemed overworked and disconnected from their guests.

The location, while prime for its own sake, is more than made up for by the hotel's numerous shortcomings.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Omni hotel. From the moment we arrived, the constant noise from the hallway and neighboring rooms made it impossible to relax. The staff seemed overwhelmed, with long lines at check-in and a gruff receptionist who didn't even bother to smile. Despite being touted as a 'prime' location in downtown, I found myself stuck in traffic both entering and exiting the hotel, which added insult to injury. Our room was tidy enough, but the housekeeping staff clearly didn't bother with details like wiping down surfaces or replenishing toilet paper rolls. And don't even get me started on the lackluster continental breakfast spread - stale pastries and lukewarm coffee. For a luxury hotel, I expected far more attention to detail and a genuine effort to provide a pleasant stay.

I recently stayed at The Palmer Hotel for a few nights and was thoroughly underwhelmed by my experience.
